Hi Alex,

Thanks for the details and the snapshot — helpful. High-level guidance and specific asks we need to size Dedicated and autoscaling behavior: 

1) SDK & Auth - SDK: Redwood provides official SDKs (Python, Node) that support both streaming and structured output (tool-calling). We recommend starting with our Python SDK for server-side integration and Node for frontend edge proxies.
- Auth: For Dedicated we support customer KMS integration and short-lived tokens issued by your identity plane. We typically recommend:
  a) Bring-your-own-KMS for key material + Redwood-managed short-lived service tokens for runtime.
  b) If you want full on-prem key control, we support HSM integrations (longer setup).

2) Routing & Regions - You can pin requests to Dedicated clusters in us-east-1. For hybrid routing (hosted fallback), we can configure policy: primary -> Dedicated pool; fallback -> hosted model variant (lower-cost) if capacity constrained. We'll provide a routing policy template in the runbook.

3) Structured output / Tool calling - Our runtime supports structured JSON outputs and tool-calling APIs. For tool-calling, we recommend moving deterministic tools (DB lookups, enrichment calls) out of model responses and wiring them via function handlers in the SDK. We'll share example handler code.

4) Embeddings & Reranker - For your rerank pipeline, recommended pattern: generate embeddings in Dedicated, store vectors in your vector DB (we support drift detection hooks), run approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) to surface candidates, then call a reranker model hosted on Dedicated with top-K candidates. For throughput sizing: reranker calls are sensitive to batch size — we suggest batching 8-16 examples per GPU for cost/latency tradeoffs.

5) Dedicated capacity & autoscaling checklist - Based on your numbers, rough starting config:
  - Min pool: capacity to serve ~300 concurrent sessions (buffer)
  - Max pool: capacity for peak ~1,500 concurrent sessions
  - Target concurrency per GPU: depends on model; for Llama2-like decoder models we estimate 1-4 concurrent streams per A100/80GB equivalent depending on token rate.
  - Batching policy: dynamic batching with max latency cap 200ms for interactive route, larger batch windows allowed for rerank/batch jobs.
  - Queueing: per-route request queues with backpressure + FIFO for batch windowing. Configure a soft queue limit (e.g., 2x expected burst) and a hard reject policy to prevent head-of-line blocking.
  - Autoscale triggers: CPU/GPU utilization + queue depth + tail latency. We prefer multi-dimensional triggers: scale up when GPU util > 70% OR queue depth > 200 OR p95 latency > SLA. Scale down conservatively with cooldown (10-15m) to avoid flapping.

6) Metrics & logs we need from you - If you can provide:
  - 1-minute QPS, 1-minute concurrent sessions, token/sec, average/95/99 latency per route, and sample payload sizes.
  - Network egress/proxy details and firewall IP CIDRs (we'll request exceptions).

Next steps (technical):
- Alex/FinServe: share the capacity snapshot + firewall/IP constraints (you mentioned NAT/proxy).
- Marissa/Dev: we'll prepare a runbook with routing policy, SDK example for embeddings->ANN->reranker, and an initial Dedicated sizing proposal based on your snapshot.
